info.name: AI Gateway - oauth2 policy
info.description:
End-to-end test collection for the oauth2 dev policy - grant-type agnostic (client_credentials and password both implemented), with a Redis-backed token cache shared across gateway-runtime replicas.

Companion to gateway/dev-policies/oauth2-generator/e2e/TESTING.md - read that doc for the full narrative; this collection is the same flows as importable requests.

Prerequisites before running any folder here:
1. Start both mocks (see TESTING.md Part A):
   cd gateway/dev-policies/oauth2-generator/e2e/mocks/mock-oauth2-idp && GOWORK=off go run .
   cd gateway/dev-policies/oauth2-generator/e2e/mocks/mock-ai-backend && GOWORK=off go run .
2. Build the gateway with the policy included (Part B): cd gateway && make build
3. Bring up gateway-controller + gateway-runtime (Part C) via gateway/docker-compose.yaml. Add --profile redis (and list the redis service) if you want folder 04's Redis verification to have something to check:
   docker compose --profile redis up -d gateway-controller gateway-runtime sample-backend redis

IMPORTANT: requests to {{gatewayBaseUrl}} use a self-signed certificate (this mirrors curl's -k flag in TESTING.md). In Postman, disable 'SSL certificate verification' under Settings > General, or these requests will fail with a TLS error unrelated to the policy itself.

Run folders in order: 00 (health) -> 01 (register the AI APIs) -> 02/03 (test flows) -> 04 (Redis token cache verification, optional) -> 05 (cleanup).

mock-oauth2-idp (run natively on host via go run)
mock-ai-backend (run natively on host via go run)

mock-ai-backend instance dedicated to E.35's model-failover PRIMARY target (run natively on host via go run, ADDR=:9604) - a second instance of the same binary as backendBaseUrl, never shared with it.
mock-ai-backend instance dedicated to E.35's model-failover FALLBACK target (run natively on host via go run, ADDR=:9605).
mock-forward-proxy (run natively on host via go run) - only used by E.26 (proxyURL)
E.33 only (manual, opt-in): a REAL OAuth2 token endpoint (e.g. an Asgardeo tenant's https://api.<region>.asgardeo.io/t/<org>/oauth2/token). Leave empty to skip E.33 - it is never run by run-e2e.sh.
E.33 only: the real IdP client_credentials Client ID. Never commit a real value here.
E.33 only: the real IdP client_credentials Client Secret. Never commit a real value here.

E.33 only: the real backend the generated token is forwarded to. Default is Postman's own public echo service (no auth of its own - proves token fetch/injection/delivery, not IdP-side validation). Pair with realWorldBackendPath.
E.33 only: path on realWorldBackendUrl to call - /headers on postman-echo.com echoes back the received Authorization header.

item.name: 01 - Register AI APIs (LLM Providers)
item.description: Registers all six LlmProviders used by the test flows below, each using the typed upstream.auth.type: oauth2 field (no generic policies list needed).

request.description: Happy-path provider for E.1 and E.2 (caching).

item.name: E.35a - Combined: merged RetryPolicy (model-failover + resilience.retry) + oauth2-generator's self-retry leg
item.description:
Part 1/2 of E.35 (see E.35b for part 2) - split into two folders/newman invocations with a real sleep >= suspendDuration (10s) between them, the same pattern E.32a/E.32b uses, because model-failover records a suspend on whichever target received the FAILED attempt of ANY native Envoy retry on this route - even one triggered by oauth2-generator's own self-retry (401 token-purge), which is NOT one of model-failover's own configured statusCodes:[500]. Running both legs back-to-back in one folder was empirically observed to make E.35b's force-500-on-primary check silently skip primary (still suspended from E.35a's own retry), landing on fallback instead and failing an assertion that primary was ever dialed. This is a genuine, worth-documenting cross-policy interaction: an Envoy-level retry the policy-engine dispatches through model-failover's own AttemptCount-indexed target selection affects model-failover's suspend bookkeeping regardless of which policy's trigger caused that retry.

Registers oauth2-test-mf-combined (see '01' folder) with all three of: upstream.auth type oauth2 (default tokenPurgeStatusCodes:[401]), a model-failover policy (retry-source, statusCodes:[500]), AND an explicit resilience.retry:{statusCodes:[503]} block - all on the same operation. resilience.retry's code (503) is deliberately DISJOINT from oauth2-generator's own tokenPurgeStatusCodes ([401]) - EMPIRICALLY CONFIRMED NECESSARY: an earlier version of this test used resilience.retry:{401}, the same code oauth2-generator's own self-retry watches, and it failed consistently. Root cause: once 401 is in the route's merged Envoy RetryPolicy, Envoy's OWN native retry can resolve a 401 by dispatching to the next aggregate-cluster priority target BEFORE oauth2-generator's downstream/listener-scoped response-phase ext_proc logic (which is what does the actual token purge+refetch) ever sees the failure - ext_proc's response phase only observes the FINAL response after Envoy's own retry loop already completed. If that retry happens to land on a target that returns 200 regardless of the (still revoked) token's validity, the client sees a clean 200 with NO fresh token ever fetched - the self-retry purge/refetch simply never runs. This is a real, worth-knowing precedence gotcha for anyone combining resilience.retry with a policy's own response-phase self-retry mechanism on the same status code - avoid the overlap, as this registration now does. Proves, with that overlap avoided: (1) registration succeeds - an explicit resilience.retry alongside a retry-source policy (model-failover) on the same operation is no longer rejected, it composes via MergeRetryConditions; (2) gateway-controller merges model-failover's statusCodes:[500] and resilience.retry's statusCodes:[503] into exactly ONE Envoy RouteAction.RetryPolicy whose retriable_status_codes contains both 500 and 503 - oauth2-generator itself contributes nothing to that merge, since its token-purge retry is an independent, Envoy-untouched self-retry (see E.34); (3) oauth2's own self-retry (401, revoked token) still fires correctly and gets a genuinely fresh, non-revoked token on whichever attempt actually serves the response - the retry is NOT guaranteed to land back on primary, since it's dispatched through model-failover's own aggregate-cluster priority mechanism (see 'Invoke the API again...' request's own description for the full explanation).

item.name: E.33 - Real-world OAuth2 verification against YOUR OWN IdP (opt-in: RUN_REALWORLD_TEST=1 ./run-e2e.sh, or standalone newman/Postman)
item.description:
Attaches oauth2-generator directly to a plain RestApi (via policies:, not an LLM/MCP upstream.auth convenience field - the one attachment path E.1-E.32 never covered) and points it at a real, live OAuth2 token endpoint you control (e.g. an Asgardeo M2M application's client_credentials grant), forwarding to a real backend.

Before running: set realWorldTokenEndpoint/realWorldClientId/realWorldClientSecret in a Postman ENVIRONMENT (not this collection's own variables, and never commit real values) to your own IdP's details. realWorldBackendUrl/realWorldBackendPath default to postman-echo.com/headers, which needs no setup of its own and just echoes back the Authorization header it received - proof of token fetch + injection + delivery, not IdP-side token validation.

Run order: Register -> Send request -> Delete (always run Delete after, even if Send request fails - the registration holds your real client secret in the controller's store until removed).

Verified live 2026-08-07 against a real Asgardeo tenant: real client_credentials token fetch, real header injection to postman-echo.com, 200 OK with the real Bearer token echoed back.

Off by default in run-e2e.sh (opt in with RUN_REALWORLD_TEST=1) since, unlike every other flow in this collection, it depends on real internet access to a third-party IdP and reuses one real credential across every run - see run-e2e.sh's own E.33 section for how it absorbs the Register->Send xDS propagation gap (--delay-request, with retries) when run as a single automated invocation. Running it standalone one item at a time in the Postman GUI still works too: Register -> wait 5-10s -> Send request -> Delete. Always run Delete, even if Send request still 404s - the registration holds your real client secret in the controller's store until removed.
